bundle_label: remaining-phases-2026-11-12 (continued from existing audit naming; UTC execution date is 2026-11-11)
scope: All remaining Phases 3–5; 18 groups in user-provided order

findings.title: Unify waiver and not-applicable semantics
findings.observed: R02 shows optional requirements always enter two-approval pending state. R03 countersigns NOT_APPLICABLE but stores requirement status WAIVED. Three implementations (requestWaiver, waiveRequirement and V021Workflows) follow different rules; the HTTP path uses the first.
findings.correction: Use one canonical typed waiver command/state machine. Preserve WAIVE versus NOT_APPLICABLE, actual mandatory metadata, required reason/evidence, distinct current approvers and explicit approve/reject/cancel decisions. Retire unused alternative implementations after caller migration.
findings.acceptance: Run real routes for optional/mandatory WAIVE and NA, same-person rejection, wrong role, denied evidence, rejection/reset and exports. All records, readiness and package labels must agree.

findings.title: Fence waivers and requirement changes by lifecycle and obligation revision
findings.observed: R01 creates a waiver in a CLOSED project. The public waiver methods lock a requirement/waiver but not the shared project lifecycle row; they do not bind a decision to a specific obligation revision or current supersession state.
findings.correction: Lock project then current obligation/waiver in a consistent order; require formal reopening for baseline changes and bind approval to the exact obligation version. Invalidate pending/active exceptions when protected material scope changes, retaining history.
findings.acceptance: Race closure/change-request approval/snapshot replacement with request and countersign. Closed, superseded and stale-version mutations reject atomically; approved active-project changes retain safe serial behavior.

findings.title: Make waiver retries and audit outcomes durable

source.symbol: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE

findings.observed: R04 creates two pending waivers for one requirement by repeating the service request. The public request/countersign implementations produce no corresponding business audit/outbox emission. The latest-by-requirement alias can choose a different waiver than the user reviewed.
findings.correction: Add command identity/version preconditions and an explicit one-current-intent policy. Address decisions by waiver ID; return the prior outcome for identical retries and reject conflicting payloads. Emit secret-free business events transactionally.
findings.acceptance: Test parallel/replayed requests, lost response after commit, older waiver alias, multiple pending history, rollback and countersign retry; verify one outcome and attributable audit.

findings.title: Deliver requirement assignment and the complete obligation contract
findings.observed: The create/list surface does not provide the full supported owner/member/party assignment, due/validity/naming/reuse and reviewer lifecycle. Generic creation/import is not a complete current-responsibility workflow; many records remain unassigned without a supported eligibility-controlled command.
findings.correction: Implement validated requirement editing/assignment DTOs with current identity/party/project eligibility, due-at NULL semantics and immutable revision history. Material changes use G06 approved impact control; cosmetic changes have an explicit policy.
findings.acceptance: Test member/party/unassigned transitions, departed/guest principals, invalid dates/roles, concurrent assignment and closed-project cases. Verify work queues and reminders reflect the actual current owner.

findings.title: Select one qualified evidence version consistently across consumers

source.symbol: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_requirements

findings.observed: The schema permits multiple document links per requirement; readiness uses any qualifying evidence while package creation aggregates version IDs. Status-only progress views and commercial/asset queries have additional duplicated qualification predicates.
findings.correction: Define one authoritative single-evidence MVP selection/qualification contract with doc-type, asset scope, immutable bytes, current review, expiry and revalidation. Reuse it for progress, package manifests and readiness, while retaining links/history separately.
findings.acceptance: Exercise multiple same-type links, wrong type, deleted/superseded/expired versions, shared asset manuals and conflicting revalidations. The selected version and displayed completion must match on every surface.

findings.title: Apply real snapshot lineage and approved active changes
findings.observed: Checklist import/template/create writers allow active baselines to change without the complete approved impact/version contract. Phase2 already records the resolver/lineage defects; this group owns resulting requirement revisions and exception/acceptance invalidation.
findings.correction: Implement PH2-G06-005/006 once, preserving current serialization and material-waiver invalidation. Persist actual source versions, rule evaluations, per-item provenance and retrievable prior requirement snapshots.
findings.acceptance: Replay approved ADD/MODIFY/REMOVE changes and compare old/new obligation IDs, links, waiver effects and accepted manifests. Direct active changes, stale approval and unknown catalogue mappings must reject.

findings.title: Validate the curated baseline against real engineering checklists
findings.observed: The specification calls the default HVAC set a hypothesis pending five real checklist validations. Synthetic authorization fixtures and a pack marked ACTIVE do not provide that engineering acceptance.
findings.correction: Obtain accountable HVAC/product review of real consultant/contractor mappings and representative scopes. Pin approved packs/catalogues; preserve honest empty/unconfigured projects instead of manufacturing a baseline.
findings.acceptance: Attach five lawful, sanitized source-checklist mappings, disagreement resolution, reviewer identity/date and application-level evidence/waiver/package scenarios on the final integrated SHA.

findings.title: Make atomic asset import actually atomic and preview accurate
findings.observed: R42 requests atomic=true, imports a valid first row, then fails an invalid second tag; the first asset remains committed. importAssets opens an outer transaction but createAsset opens independent transactions. Preview also omits the real AssetTagSchema check and UPDATE conflict strategy does not implement a controlled update.
findings.correction: Use one transaction/client and shared project lock for atomic import, with row savepoints only for explicitly non-atomic mode. Share row validation between preview and commit; implement or reject UPDATE and bind preview to current versions.
findings.acceptance: Test a later invalid/duplicate row, DB failure, concurrent import, scope denial and retry. Atomic failure leaves zero assets/events/requirements; non-atomic mode reports exact committed rows.

findings.title: Enforce asset scope on every mutation and derived view
findings.observed: R43 proves a Site member can list only its allowed asset yet retire an asset outside stored assetIds. Retirement lacks the resource-scope check used by list/get/update. Matching/history/passport/revalidation paths also need a complete scope contract.
findings.correction: Apply current asset/resource authorization after resolving/locking each target, including retirement, lineage, history, matching and revalidation. Push filters into queries before counts/pagination and protect related old/new assets.
findings.acceptance: Use actual HTTP for narrow asset/category/date/read-only scopes and all aliases, with positive allowed targets and hidden-target negatives. Revoke/narrow authority during a transaction and verify no stale mutation or count leak.

findings.title: Validate tag PATCH and escape matching expressions
findings.observed: R05 stores tag=[ through PATCH, then matchAssetCandidates throws a regular-expression SyntaxError. Creation validates tags but update uses trim/uppercase directly and embeds tags unescaped in RegExp.
findings.correction: Use the same bounded tag normalization/schema for create, PATCH and import; reject malformed JS types before SQL. Escape literal tags in regex or use a non-regex token matcher. Preserve case-insensitive uniqueness and historical identity revisions.
findings.acceptance: Test metacharacters, whitespace, Unicode, normalized collisions and valid HVAC tags across all entry points. Matching must return controlled results and never turn persisted user data into executable patterns.

findings.title: Make retirement and replacement lineage truthful
findings.observed: R06 reports successful retirement for an unknown asset; R07 creates a replacement while silently ignoring a nonexistent predecessor. The delete path writes ASSET_DELETED without checking a matched row and does not reconcile remaining obligations.
findings.correction: Lock/validate existing predecessor and successor with current lifecycle/scope, reject self/cyclic/wrong-project lineage, and check affected row counts. Retain evidence on the predecessor and explicitly decide the status of its obligations; distinguish retire from delete.
findings.acceptance: Test nonexistent/already-retired assets, concurrent replacements, cycles, approved evidence and obligations on old equipment. History, register and generated replacement labels must remain consistent.

findings.title: Complete category-driven instantiation and asset/system metadata
findings.observed: createAsset accepts arbitrary categoryKey and can create active assets with zero instantiated requirements when no matching snapshot definition exists. The public input does not implement the complete capacity/notes/system-relationship model implied by the group and register contract.
findings.correction: Validate against installed reviewed categories, define explicit unconfigured/unmapped states, and use G06/G07 approved applicability for new/replaced assets. Implement supported capacity/unit/relationship fields with cycle/scope validation; do not invent requirements or silently classify unknown equipment.
findings.acceptance: Use approved chiller/AHU/VRF/system scenarios, unknown categories, no baseline, retired/replaced assets and relationship cycles. Verify expected per-asset obligations and honest unresolved mappings.

findings.title: Qualify revalidation decisions and preserve stale-evidence history
findings.observed: Revalidation has positive expected-version, uploader-independence and project-lock controls, but accepts a caller status/notes contract without a complete reviewed verifier qualification, exemption proof and terminal-transition policy. Native identity changes can generate many work items without an approved allocation plan.
findings.correction: Define permitted current reviewers, mandatory factual serial/location checks, reason/evidence for EXEMPT and version-bound terminal decisions. Preserve per-asset invalidation for shared documents and prevent an exemption from silently restoring unrelated acceptance.
findings.acceptance: Test wrong verifier/stage, expired evidence, status reset, no evidence for exemption, repeated identity revisions, mixed assets and concurrent updates. Retain current self-revalidation and scope-specific mismatch protections.

findings.title: Deliver usable imports, registers and scoped exports
findings.observed: The backend asset export returns JSON data rather than the promised user-ready Excel/CSV contract. Full validated CSV/Excel parsing, field mapping and dry-run error recovery are not delivered by an array-input import alone; the UI must distinguish current identities from historical/replaced units.
findings.correction: Implement bounded file parsing and typed mapping to the corrected importer, safe CSV/Excel generation, pagination and relationship/replacement visibility. Defend spreadsheet formula cells and preserve integer/unit data.
findings.acceptance: Run real UI import→preview→commit→export with duplicates, invalid tags, large files, formula-like cells and scoped users; compare exported records and failures to actual database state.

findings.title: Accept real equipment/evidence lifecycle scenarios independently
findings.observed: The audit uses synthetic assets and database records to isolate mechanics. It does not validate real equipment identity, legal replacement, OEM coverage or approved evidence after field changes.
findings.correction: On one integrated head, obtain domain review and actual browser/API/worker evidence for creation, import, replacement, relocation, revalidation and package rendering.
findings.acceptance: Use representative actual asset mappings and sanitized genuine evidence, including shared manuals and mismatched serials. Attach negative scope/concurrency and old-project preservation results.

findings.title: Count compressed PDF objects in the real upload verifier
findings.observed: R41 constructs a harmless one-page PDF with 25,014 indirect objects; the actual upload verifier returns READY. Its qpdf --show-xref count includes only lines containing offset =, omitting compressed objects. The separate PDF-engine helper has different inventory logic.
findings.correction: Use a complete bounded parsed inventory including object streams in the actual file-verification path. Apply one consistent page/object/decompression/resource policy before READY, with explicit parser timeout and memory/process limits.
findings.acceptance: Test equivalent compressed/uncompressed PDFs around each ceiling, corrupt xrefs, deeply nested/large streams and scanner failure. Over-limit documents must fail before publication; valid near-limit files must remain usable.

findings.title: Reject mutable null-version storage receipts
findings.observed: R44 calls the actual S3 finalizeUpload method with a protocol fixture returning VersionId="null" and receives it as an immutable receipt. Suspended/unversioned S3 null versions are not an immutable version identity; package output checks also rely on truthiness.
findings.correction: Validate real non-null immutable provider identities at upload, worker/output publication and signing boundaries. Reject empty/null sentinel versions and define provider capability checks before accepting traffic.
findings.acceptance: Test absent, empty, literal null and real version IDs across upload/retry/download/package output; overwrite the mutable object in a storage fixture and verify it can never become READY evidence.

findings.title: Validate container format and declared-versus-detected content
findings.observed: R36 sends a harmless malformed PK-header .docx through a clean scanner protocol fixture; the verifier returns READY with detectedMime=application/zip. The runtime path does not establish valid OOXML/container structure or declared MIME/extension compatibility. Filename macro bans alone do not inspect embedded container content.
findings.correction: Distinguish ZIP from supported OOXML via bounded structural validation and explicit file policy. Reject corrupt/mislabeled/active-macro containers and enforce entry/path/size/ratio limits before extraction or conversion. Keep scanner acknowledgement separate from structural qualification.
findings.acceptance: Test valid DOCX/XLSX/ZIP, corrupt containers, mismatched names/MIME, macro parts, nested archives and limits. Do not mark a clean scanner response as proof that a file is parseable or safe to convert.

findings.title: Fence upload lifecycle and latest-version publication
findings.observed: R08 creates an upload intent for a CLOSED project. R09 completes R1 then R0 and the document latest_version_id rewinds to R0. Completion correctly queues PROCESSING rather than pretending scan success, but state/parent publication is not ordered by the latest issued revision.
findings.correction: Use shared project/document locks and an explicit lifecycle policy for create/refresh/complete/abort. Make completion of an old intent settle its own receipt without moving the latest pointer backwards; preserve current approved version until a valid review.
findings.acceptance: Race old/new completion, closure, abort and retry. Verify one scan event/receipt, no pointer rewind, and controlled closed/archived/suspended behavior across route aliases.

findings.title: Bound provider work and reconcile upload reservations outside long locks
findings.observed: Presign/multipart creation and completion/abort invoke external storage while tenant transactions are open. Lost replies can leave an external session/object without committed DB outcome; storage quotas do not reserve pending bytes (Phase2 G18). Signed single PUT does not encode a reviewed content-length/checksum enforcement policy.
findings.correction: Persist durable intent/attempt state, perform provider work outside business locks and settle with fenced receipts. Enforce declared length/checksum using provider-supported controls and reconcile unknown outcomes, pending reservations and expired intents.
findings.acceptance: Inject slow provider, timeout after accepted multipart creation/completion, DB rollback, oversize PUT, wrong checksum and concurrent quota slots. Verify bounded DB locks and no leaked reservation or false success.

findings.title: Clean up physical orphaned uploads and enforce retention policy
findings.observed: The scheduler cleans abandoned DB upload records, while storage lifecycle/abort/delete reconciliation is not a complete provider-object cleanup workflow. Terraform supplies versioning but no full lifecycle/hold policy for abandoned multipart uploads and orphaned versions.
findings.correction: Add a durable, least-privilege physical cleanup/reconciliation process with verified ownership, grace periods and hold/retention checks. Separate abandoned temporary uploads from retained evidence and keep failed cleanup observable/retryable.
findings.acceptance: Test crash between each provider/DB step, abandoned multipart, unknown objects, legal hold and retry. Prove only intended temporary versions are removed and retained customer evidence remains recoverable.

findings.title: Contain scanner and converter resource/identity boundaries
findings.observed: Current verification has checksum, magic, scanner fail-closed and bounded qpdf calls. Scanner sockets accumulate responses and do not provide a complete process/container/network sandbox contract; LibreOffice/ImageMagick conversion is a worker subprocess with a separate user directory, not an OS security sandbox.
findings.correction: Run parsers/converters under reviewed non-root isolated execution with CPU/memory/time/output/network limits and bounded scanner protocol responses. Verify scanner database freshness/readiness and separate runtime credentials by service; never enable test scan bypass in production.
findings.acceptance: Test process OOM/hang, malformed scanner replies, expired signatures, parser output bombs, egress attempts in an isolated test and shutdown. Failure must stay quarantined/failed and retry only under the approved policy.

findings.title: Accept real storage/scanner uploads and interrupted transfers
findings.observed: Fake presigner, loopback scanner and programmable storage fixtures do not establish real S3/ClamAV acceptance. The existing transport tests are valuable but cannot certify sender credentials, live object versioning, CORS or production-size interruption recovery.
findings.correction: Obtain actual provider/scanner and operational acceptance using isolated approved infrastructure, least-privilege IAM, versioning, checksums and scanner definitions. Keep production enablement blocked until verified.
findings.acceptance: Run browser multipart interruption/resume, ETag/CORS, same-size corruption, wrong version, malware test sample, scanner outage and large-file budgets with sanitized real receipts on the final head.

findings.title: Repair delete/restore quota SQL in the actual document service
findings.observed: R10 and R11 reproduce SQLSTATE42804: the document delete/restore methods assign text expressions to BIGINT usage_counters.value. The shared quota helper repair in Phase1 did not repair these duplicate statements; transactions roll back.
findings.correction: Use the authoritative typed quota settlement helper and per-object reservation/accounting identity. Preserve original failures and avoid double refund/re-add across shared objects, retries, status changes and restores.
findings.acceptance: Test actual HTTP delete/restore with nonzero READY bytes, repeated commands, shared references, concurrent scan finalization and rollback. Counter deltas must occur exactly once without bypassing plan limits.

findings.title: Protect evidence deletion/restoration with lifecycle and retention locks
findings.observed: R12 soft-deletes a record from a CLOSED project. Delete/restore lack the shared project/retention/hold policy and do not record the full actor/reason/history. Retained package or accepted evidence cannot be governed solely by a deleted_at toggle.
findings.correction: Define approved soft-delete, restore and restricted correction rules under project/document locks, retention/hold and package-reference checks. Preserve immutable objects and historical evidence; formal reopening is required for material baseline changes.
findings.acceptance: Test accepted/packaged evidence, closed/archived projects, legal holds, stale versions and concurrent review/package generation. Rejected deletion has no quota/audit side effects; authorized restoration has valid capacity.

findings.title: Complete typed metadata and revision management
findings.observed: The document controller/service has upload/replace/read/delete/restore but no complete runtime-validated metadata editing/history contract. Revision, issue/expiry, type/category, owner and notes have different validation coverage; several date/type inputs remain strings and unknown catalogue types can enter through unlinked uploads.
findings.correction: Implement the supported metadata API with version preconditions, bounded valid dates/enums and explicit nullable clearing. Preserve per-version immutable evidence, supersedes links, distinct internal/external notes and an auditable correction policy.
findings.acceptance: Test full round trips, invalid JS types/dates, missing/mismatched types, revision-code collisions and new revision versus clerical correction. Evidence qualification must update only through approved review/impact rules.

findings.title: Keep linking, upload and qualification as distinct states
findings.observed: Batch linking now checks project lifecycle, target scope/type and guest ownership, which is positive. Its verifiedEvidence response and UPLOADED transition rely on latest file_status=READY rather than the full immutable-object qualification used by final readiness; linked history must not become a claim of approval.
findings.correction: Reuse shared verified-byte predicates for every verified label, preserve explicit linked/uploaded/approved states and select the qualifying version deterministically. Audit link/unlink/material scope changes and invalidate affected exceptions/acceptance when required.
findings.acceptance: Test READY-marker-without-receipt, wrong type/asset, deleted/superseded versions, one document shared by assets and link changes after acceptance. Preserve the current guest-scope and lifecycle negative controls.

findings.title: Finish bulk import and transmittal response workflows honestly
findings.observed: Bulk ZIP import and legacy stamp-back correctly return unavailable rather than fake success. Transmittal creation persists a DRAFT register but does not deliver the complete import/preview/commit or authority-checked response journey promised by their contracts.
findings.correction: Keep retired unsafe routes closed. Implement bounded file-based import with mapping/dry-run/commit receipts and a canonical per-item transmittal response command pinned to exact versions and independently verified external proof.
findings.acceptance: Run corrupt ZIP/duplicate/large import rollback and real user preview/error recovery. Record external responses against persisted items; old arbitrary-version stamp-back remains denied.

findings.title: Deliver permission-filtered metadata search and scalable registers
findings.observed: There is no dedicated global metadata search/report API implementing all required search/filter/export dimensions. Existing lists and frontend local filtering do not provide global query-time permission filtering, stable paging and scoped exports across documents/requirements.
findings.correction: Implement parameterized permission-scoped search and paginated typed registers for the approved metadata-only MVP, with consistent filters/counts and safe exports. Defer extracted full-text/saved views according to V1 scope.
findings.acceptance: Test cross-tenant/project/resource negatives, no-result versus denied behavior, stable pagination during writes and each documented filter; export must match visible query scope.

findings.title: Accept complete document/revision journeys with real verified bytes
findings.observed: Synthetic database markers exercise mechanics, not end-user acceptance of real immutable documents. Existing browser tests do not cover the complete upload→scan→metadata→review→revision→package→retained download flow.
findings.correction: Run the full production-built application journey against approved isolated storage/scanner services and a reviewed baseline, with independently inspected artifacts/history.
findings.acceptance: Include rejection/resubmission, upload interruption, metadata corrections, deleted/expired evidence, multi-asset links, access changes and retained accepted-package download on the final integrated SHA.

findings.title: Validate and complete the party register
findings.observed: R13 stores an unknown party type and invalid email. createParty trims strings and defaults types without a complete runtime schema; the controller has no full update/contact/status/import lifecycle for the required party model.
findings.correction: Implement bounded validated party/contact/type/GST/address DTOs, canonical destinations and authorized versioned CRUD/import. Define duplicate/merge/archive behavior and revoke downstream authority when the counterparty relationship changes.
findings.acceptance: Test invalid types/contacts/GST, omission/clearing, duplicate imports, wrong tenant, concurrent archive and references from projects/grants/submissions. A contact entry must not itself establish external authority.

findings.title: Complete independently verified counterparty delegation
findings.observed: Guest OTP, distinct guest principals, fixed capability profiles and current client/consultant project binding are meaningful protections. Issuing an OTP destination still does not prove lawful party representation; the privileged approval scripts are not a complete accountable user/delegation workflow.
findings.correction: Deliver the reviewed independent counterparty onboarding/delegation/expiry/revocation workflow with current principal, contact evidence and constrained reviewer authority. Preserve G01 independent-authority fences; do not let contractor-managed contacts self-mint acceptance/witness rights.
findings.acceptance: Test spoofed contacts, wrong project/party/type, expired or revoked delegation, account/contact change and two reviewers. Legitimate real external representatives must complete supported tasks without weakening proof.

findings.title: Apply procurement lifecycle and field validation
findings.observed: R14 creates an ISSUED procurement order with zero lines in a CLOSED project. The writer lacks the shared project-state lock, full bounded line/quantity/money/type validation and business audit emission.
findings.correction: Implement an explicit draft/issue/change/cancel policy under the project lock, validated eligible supplier and project-bound line/asset references. Require meaningful lines and integer paise, and audit obligation creation/change without inventing engineering mappings.
findings.acceptance: Test empty/invalid/huge imports, wrong supplier/asset/project, zero/negative quantities, closed/cancelled projects and concurrent closure. Atomic failure leaves no order/line/obligation fragments.

findings.title: Persist supplier intake decisions and rejection history
findings.observed: Current intake correctly requires contractor authority, project lock and supplier/project/type-qualified evidence; acceptance is explicitly not engineering approval. Rejection only sets PENDING and returns notes without durable decision/reason history, while acceptance also lacks its business audit event.
findings.correction: Add a versioned intake decision ledger and transactional safe events. Keep submitted evidence/rejection reasons attributable, allow a clear resubmission transition and separate intake from engineering qualification.
findings.acceptance: Test accepted retry, rejected/reuploaded versions, supplier mismatch, proof-byte failure, concurrent decisions and rollback. The UI and supplier task must show the saved reason/history, not only a transient response.

findings.title: Finish external-party application journeys and scoped responses
findings.observed: The guest context/read contracts have been narrowed and package acceptance/witness actions are guarded, but the web guest page does not deliver all required review, independently authenticated witness, submission-response and recovery journeys. Missing UI is not repaired by capability strings.
findings.correction: Build supported guest tasks around current verified grant/principal context, safe projections and exact resource IDs. Provide honest unavailable/blocked states, recipient-specific links, expiry/revocation recovery and safe support contact.
findings.acceptance: Use actual browsers for supplier/client/consultant, wrong party/contact, forwarded link, stale tabs, removed scope and failed delivery. No private reviewer identities/comments or contractor-only package content may leak.

findings.title: Define party/grant lifecycle cleanup and safe audits
findings.observed: Grant revoke/session fences exist, but full party status/contact changes, project relationship changes and retained historical authority need one explicit lifecycle and audit policy. Raw invite URLs or OTP destinations must not be treated as general public party data.
findings.correction: Implement versioned counterparty/grant transitions with narrow safe audit projection and derived-session revocation/revalidation. Preserve historical signer/recipient facts while preventing future use of retired relationships.
findings.acceptance: Race party archive/contact change/project reassignment with login and decision. Verify active tasks stop safely, history remains attributable and no bearer URL/OTP/provider secret reaches logs or exports.

findings.title: Accept real external representatives and delivery operationally
findings.observed: No fixture can establish legal delegation, real OTP delivery or a genuine customer/supplier acceptance. Source restrictions can be sound while legitimate onboarding remains operationally unavailable.
findings.correction: Obtain accountable counterparty/privacy/domain approval and real provider/browser evidence for each supported external task. Keep authority activation blocked until the independent process is accepted.
findings.acceptance: Attach sanitized delegation/proof provenance, provider outcomes and wrong-party/revocation negatives on the final head; distinguish attendance, review attestation, cryptographic signature and contractual acceptance.

findings.title: Filter work items and counts by resource/action visibility
findings.observed: R19 gives a Site member scope for asset A; listWorkItems still returns the hidden asset B defect and includes it in counts. The union scopes by project membership, not each resource, review assignment or next-command capability.
findings.correction: Build each queue branch from current eligible actor/assignment/resource predicates before union/count/pagination. Return only safe DTOs and actions the actor may currently perform; do not leak reasons through unavailable commands.
findings.acceptance: Test narrowed assets/requirements/documents, read-only roles, unassigned reviews, expired grants and scope changes. List, counts and command eligibility must agree under real HTTP negatives.

findings.title: Implement eligible assignment, delegation and operational successors
findings.observed: The queue is a union of domain records rather than a complete responsibility engine. Required owner/party, reviewer, pending submission, package and defect succession are not uniformly representable; G03 gap handling still blocks or omits several categories.
findings.correction: Introduce explicit operational assignment and versioned per-work allocation/delegation separate from immutable authorship. Validate current project/role/stage/resource eligibility and preserve dependencies when an owner leaves.
findings.acceptance: Exercise assign/unassign/delegate/offboard across requirements, reviews, supplier obligations, defects and submissions. Block incompatible successors with an accurate actionable manifest and no orphaned active work.

findings.title: Retire duplicate legacy workflow implementations
findings.observed: V021WorkflowsService and executeReviewDecision are used by simulation scripts rather than the current HTTP canonical path. Their waiver/review/recipient semantics diverge, so simulation success cannot certify actual route behavior. Database external-authority protections may correctly reject old helpers.
findings.correction: Inventory every caller, migrate supported scripts and routes to canonical transaction-aware commands and remove or explicitly quarantine legacy helpers. Share one state vocabulary and qualification contract; never weaken DB constraints to revive simulations.
findings.acceptance: Trace every workflow button and script to its actual command. Run the same positive/negative fixtures through supported entry points and verify no legacy path bypasses current authority, lifecycle or version rules.

findings.title: Make action contracts versioned and recoverable
findings.observed: Work items expose nextCommand and sometimes entityVersion, but different commands require different preconditions/reasons/evidence and the queue has no complete typed execution contract. Waiver/obligation items use constant version=1; unsupported actions can be advertised.
findings.correction: Expose a typed available-action schema with actual entity/precondition, required fields, current assignee and blocking reason. Implement one recoverable command client with stable idempotency, stale-item refresh and domain-specific validation.
findings.acceptance: Execute every advertised command from the real UI, including stale versions, lost response, actor switch and denied authority. A queue item may not report done before committed domain acknowledgement.

findings.title: Coordinate business transitions, audit and durable events
findings.observed: Several current domain commands change state without a business event, while shared outbox dispatch has new claims/retry controls. Durable transport cannot recover a business event that was never emitted or an assignment spread across independently committed commands.
findings.correction: Define transaction/event ownership for each supported workflow and include safe causation/command/version IDs. Use one transaction for atomic transitions and a reviewed saga only where external outcomes require it; reconcile partial/unknown states explicitly.
findings.acceptance: Inject failure between each state/event/provider boundary, replay events and restart consumers. Reconstruct each user-visible outcome from the authoritative records without duplicate responsibility transfer or hidden success.

findings.title: Provide complete due/SLA and exception handling for current work
findings.observed: WorkItem supports dueAt but mapping does not populate it; current union covers only selected review/waiver/defect/revalidation/intake states. Missing ownership, pending customer response and approved deferred technical work lack a complete actionable responsibility view.
findings.correction: Implement reviewed MVP task categories and due semantics, explicit unresolved assignment/exception states and safe owner recovery. Scope optional escalation/SLA/delegation enhancements as V1 without hiding required unresolved work.
findings.acceptance: Compare queues to canonical domain counts with NULL/future/past due values, disabled users and partially accepted submissions. Verify deterministic paging and useful recovery when no eligible person exists.

findings.title: Accept end-to-end responsibility recovery and distributed failures
findings.observed: Current local tests do not prove complete responsibility transfer or recovery across multiple API/worker instances and real browser interruptions.
findings.correction: Run the integrated workflow matrix with independent review of authority, lifecycle locks, causation and user recovery. Preserve immutable provenance and external-party authority.
findings.acceptance: Include simultaneous offboarding/decision/closure, worker redelivery, provider timeout and reload, with no orphaned work, fabricated approval or unbounded silent retries.

findings.title: Make the first terminal document decision win across assignments
findings.observed: R38 approves version V via assigned review A, then rejects V through another assigned review. Both succeed; V becomes REJECTED while documents.current_approved_version_id still points to V. Locking each review/version does not enforce a terminal decision across sibling assignments.
findings.correction: Under the canonical document/version lock, enforce current submission/stage state and one terminal outcome for the configured stage model. Cancel/settle sibling assignments consistently; permit corrections only through a separately authorized audited override with reason.
findings.acceptance: Race two reviewers and serial conflicting decisions on the same version, including approve/reject/change. Exactly one ordinary terminal outcome wins; pointers, requirements, package eligibility and history stay coherent.

findings.title: Validate submission eligibility before creating a review
findings.observed: R15 submits an expired READY-marker version without immutable provider metadata. The public submitReview path does not share the full metadata/expiry/byte-verification checks used elsewhere. It also lacks the project lifecycle lock.
findings.correction: Use one locked submission command validating current exact revision, required metadata, not-expired evidence, immutable verified bytes, matching requirement type/scope and project state. Preserve current project/type authority and prevent duplicate submittals.
findings.acceptance: Test expired, unscanned/marker-only, wrong type, superseded/deleted, closed project and repeated submissions. Qualified evidence enters the intended review exactly once.

findings.title: Assign a real eligible reviewer instead of the submitting actor
findings.observed: R16 submits an uploader-owned document; submitReview assigns that same user, then approval correctly fails self-approval. There is no complete eligible reviewer assignment/delegation journey to resolve this queue through supported actions.
findings.correction: Derive required stage/role from the approved obligation/configuration and assign a current eligible independent reviewer. Model unassigned/blocked queues honestly and provide controlled assignment/delegation without letting decision create authority.
findings.acceptance: Run uploader, role-qualified reviewer, no eligible reviewer, departed reviewer and narrowed scope cases through the UI. Preserve self-approval denial and prevent arbitrary actors from minting their own assignment.

findings.title: Update requirement and review state coherently on every outcome
findings.observed: R18 rejects an assigned review but its linked requirement remains IN_REVIEW. Approval broadly updates linked requirements, while rejection/change and resubmission follow different paths. R17 also commits a rejection after project closure.
findings.correction: Use one transaction under project/document/obligation locks to apply outcome, current version pointer and scoped requirement effects. Reject unauthorized baseline changes after closure; distinguish historical records and approved post-close corrections explicitly.
findings.acceptance: Test approve/reject/request-changes, multiple linked requirements, current/superseded versions, closure races and notification failure. Requirement/task/UI status must reflect the committed outcome.

findings.title: Require consistent version and runtime decision validation on all routes
findings.observed: The version-decision alias validates a mapped decision but permits an omitted version via fallback; direct review and bulk APIs have different DTO/precondition behavior. Service validation checks comments only for explicit known decisions, leaving some invalid values to DB constraint failures.
findings.correction: Use one strict bounded decision DTO and mandatory actual version/precondition across supported aliases. Bind idempotency to exact version/stage and require actor-entered reasons for negative/override decisions; reject malformed types before SQL.
findings.acceptance: Exercise every HTTP alias with missing/stale/current versions, invalid enum/null/objects, oversized bulk arrays and conflicting replay keys. Return controlled 4xx and no partial audit/state on rejection.

findings.title: Enforce safe review queue, comment and annotation projections
findings.observed: getReview returns raw review/version metadata plus all comments; addComment accepts visibility and page fields without a complete role/visibility/coordinate contract. The special guest version-detail DTO is safer, but other review routes and member resource scopes need equivalent boundary coverage.
findings.correction: Apply current assignment/resource and field visibility for all read/comment/export endpoints. Validate visibility/page/coordinate/body limits, preserve immutable author identity and define who may create/read INTERNAL versus external comments.
findings.acceptance: Test client/consultant/supplier/member negatives on all aliases, narrowed resources, private comments, cross-review IDs and invalid page pins. Counts, previews and exports must not disclose hidden remarks.

findings.title: Keep advanced stages, overrides and external response paths explicit
findings.observed: MVP is single-stage; full sequential/parallel stages, override/delegation and SLA authoring are V1. Legacy helpers and partially exposed routes use different policy. Independent external approval infrastructure exists, but it is not a complete ordinary user response workflow.
findings.correction: Implement the approved single-stage contract fully and disable unsupported advanced paths honestly. Route external responses through exact-version/transmittal/proof authority, and add advanced stages/overrides only with explicit configured transition and reviewer policy.
findings.acceptance: Prove unsupported features fail safely; test legitimate independent external proof, spoofed metadata, stale revision and revoked delegation through the actual UI/API. No helper or uploaded stamp can substitute for external authority.

findings.title: Accept real independent review and immutable history journeys
findings.observed: Fixture approvals and passing API suites do not establish real reviewed evidence, reviewer competence, external legal authority or complete user recovery.
findings.correction: After repairs, independently validate full submission/review/revision/override scope on the integrated head with genuinely verified bytes and approved role assignments.
findings.acceptance: Attach actual browser flows, conflicting-review races, expired/companion negatives, exact-version external attestations and package approval-history checks. Keep legal/provider evidence separate from local fixtures.

findings.title: Reject caller-minted verified witness fields at inspection creation
findings.observed: R37 uses ordinary inspection creation to persist witnessParties containing isVerified=true, AUTHENTICATED_ATTESTATION and another signedByUserId. The dedicated witness endpoint is protected, but the creation path serializes arbitrary runtime objects wholesale. This proves forged verified-looking metadata, not that it legally closes a project.
findings.correction: Validate and allowlist creation-time witness assignments; reserve all verification/signature/principal/time fields for the trusted attestation command. Quarantine ambiguous existing records with provenance review rather than treating flags as evidence.
findings.acceptance: Use actual HTTP member creation with injected/nested signature fields and typed legitimate assignments. Caller fields must reject or be safely discarded; only independently authenticated witness transitions may create authoritative verification records.

findings.title: Bind attestations to an exact immutable inspection and declaration
findings.observed: The dedicated witness command checks active independent party authority and assignment and distinguishes attendance, which is positive. Its record is a JSON witness append without a complete content digest/version/declaration and fresh-assurance contract for precisely what was attested.
findings.correction: Create an immutable attestation record bound to inspection/evidence revision, digest, declared scope, trusted principal/delegation and proof time. Capture explicit informed consent; material inspection changes require a new version and re-attestation, not mutation of old claims.
findings.acceptance: Test stale/changed content, wrong party/revision, repeated signing, expired proof, revoked delegation and attendance-only records. Verify export/UI identifies exact attested content and never relabels attendance as a signature.

findings.title: Complete independently reviewed external evidence and recovery workflows
findings.observed: G01 supplies restricted authority/proof scripts and DB fences, but legal delegation review, per-document attestation, expiry/revocation/correction and legitimate customer recovery are not a complete accepted business process.
findings.correction: Provide a reviewed role-separated operational workflow for authority and exact-document evidence, including safe revocation and preservation of past facts. Keep privileged verifier credentials outside ordinary runtime and separate OTP identity from party representation.
findings.acceptance: Run two accountable reviewers/representatives, wrong subject/hash/version, revocation after proof, backdated records and recovery. Preserve current database refusal of contractor self-minted approval.

findings.title: Keep cryptographic signing honestly disabled until a verifier exists
findings.observed: R20 confirms cryptographic record creation fails closed. Preparation/embedding also return unavailable and public verification always reports verified=false with only a possible digest match. E-sign integration is V2, so absence alone is not an MVP blocker.
findings.correction: Retain explicit disabled states and remove any UI/output implication that a digest or blank signature box is a verified signature. If V2 signing is included, implement real provider/trust-chain/revocation/timestamp validation and exact-byte signature verification before persisting certification.
findings.acceptance: Test disabled endpoints and UI, digest match/mismatch versus cryptographic validity, unsigned placeholder PDFs and provider failures. No caller-supplied certificate/PKCS7 string may become a certification.

findings.title: Define public verification privacy, input and immutable receipt policy
findings.observed: The public code endpoint directly trims code/hash and returns signer/certificate metadata for a found record. A complete bounded schema, abuse/lookup policy, trusted lookup boundary and immutable verified-record provenance must exist before using it as a public assurance channel.
findings.correction: Validate bounded code/hash inputs before DB work, define safe public projection and rate limits, and separate record existence/digest consistency from trust validity. Preserve tenant RLS with a narrowly reviewed verifier lookup rather than broad table access.
findings.acceptance: Test malformed/oversized values, enumeration budgets, wrong digest, revoked/unverified legacy records and safe not-found responses under restricted runtime. Do not infer verified trust from a row or QR code.

findings.title: Obtain real attestation and signature acceptance for the selected scope
findings.observed: No source or synthetic witness fixture proves a legal signatory, qualified external reviewer, real DSC/eSign trust chain or lawful delegation. V2 signing must remain explicitly deferred if not accepted.
findings.correction: Obtain accountable domain/legal/security review of supported attestations and any included signing provider, with independently retained evidence on the final head.
findings.acceptance: Attach real representative and proof provenance, exact-byte verification, revoked/expired/wrong-version negatives and clear user-facing distinctions among attendance, attestation, digest and cryptographic signature.

findings.title: Apply explicit lifecycle policy to technical records and planned post-close tests
findings.observed: R21/R22 record a COMPLETED TAB calculation and PASSED inspection in a CLOSED project. These methods check project existence but do not acquire/check the shared lifecycle lock. Planned seasonal testing after handover needs an explicit exception policy, not unrestricted baseline mutation.
findings.correction: Classify baseline-changing commissioning records versus approved post-handover follow-up. Lock the shared project and exact technical revision; require formal reopening for changes to accepted baseline while preserving separately authorized deferred-test history.
findings.acceptance: Race closure with TAB/inspection/seasonal create/update; test suspended/cancelled/archived and approved deferred cases. Historical package/attestation facts remain frozen and new work cannot silently change accepted evidence.

findings.title: Bind TAB calculations to reviewed design, procedure and tolerances
findings.observed: R21 computes COMPLETED from caller-entered design/actual values without a pinned approved design, method, instrument/calibration or qualified reviewer. Positive finite/unit/raw-ratio checks exist; the default 10%/maximum 15% tolerance is code policy, not evidence of the applicable contract or a universal standard.
findings.correction: Persist procedure/design revision, measurement units and operating conditions, instrument/calibration identity, qualified tester/reviewer and contract-specific tolerance. Separate calculated-within-tolerance from approved commissioning evidence; bound realistic input ranges and aggregates.
findings.acceptance: Use independently reviewed air/water/VRF/chilled-water scenarios, tolerance boundaries and just-outside values without premature rounding. Test missing/expired instruments, wrong design revision, unsupported units and unapproved procedures.

findings.title: Use approved inspection checklists and trustworthy witness assignments
findings.observed: The creator supplies arbitrary checklist descriptions/results and witness JSON. All-NA correctly remains PENDING (R24), but PASS is derived from caller rows without approved inspection revision, acceptance criteria or reviewer. R37 exposes the forged witness-field boundary separately in G12.
findings.correction: Use approved versioned ITR/checklist definitions with stable unique item IDs, required criteria, applicability and controlled results. Allowlist witness assignments and bind reviewed technical records to immutable evidence/attestation revisions.
findings.acceptance: Test duplicate/omitted items, all-NA, failed mandatory criteria, unsupported stages and injected witness fields. A local calculation or entered PASS must not become independently accepted engineering evidence.

findings.title: Enforce seasonal test transitions, result schemas and revision history
findings.observed: R23 marks a schedule PERFORMED using an arbitrary nonempty object, then resets it to SCHEDULED. The reset response can retain an old completedAt while the stored value is NULL. No actual version precondition or reviewed terminal-correction policy protects the result.
findings.correction: Define schedule/result schemas per approved procedure, required evidence, responsible tester/reviewer and an explicit transition graph. Version completed results; require controlled correction/defer/waive reasons and return committed timestamps.
findings.acceptance: Test empty/meaningless results, stale updates, terminal resets, reason-only waivers, duplicate completion and approved post-close schedules. Date/status/UI/history and downstream reminders must match.

findings.title: Enforce asset/resource eligibility on commissioning reads and writes
findings.observed: Commissioning checks exact project/asset existence but does not apply the same stored narrower asset/category scope used by AssetsService. Lists return raw readings and tester identities for all project worksheets/schedules; generic document.upload is the creation capability.
findings.correction: Define a reviewed commissioning capability/qualification policy and current resource filters for each target and derived list/count. Validate active equipment/system membership and preserve allowed external witness paths separately.
findings.acceptance: Run actual HTTP scoped Site/QC/PM/guest cases, hidden/retired/replaced assets, read-only scope and revocation during writes. Qualified allowed targets succeed without exposing other technical records.

findings.title: Connect native technical records to reviewed document and handover evidence
findings.observed: Native TAB/inspection/seasonal records are separate tables; COMPLETED/PASSED alone does not produce a verified immutable reviewed document version. The application lacks a complete issue/revise/approve/render/link journey and domain-qualified technical register.
findings.correction: Implement controlled technical report issuance with immutable source/result revision and rendered object lineage, then route it through canonical review and requirement mapping. Preserve raw readings and explicit pending/failed/unverified states.
findings.acceptance: Run capture→review→issued report→requirement→package with genuine procedure/mapping evidence. Altered readings/design/witnesses must require a new revision and appropriate requalification.

findings.title: Obtain independent HVAC commissioning acceptance
findings.observed: No synthetic reading or status fixture proves HVAC performance, calibration, witness authority or compliance with a specific consultant specification. Threshold labels in code are not independent engineering sign-off.
findings.correction: Have accountable HVAC/commissioning reviewers approve procedure/catalogue/design/tolerance mappings and real representative reports on the final head.
findings.acceptance: Attach sanitized real equipment/testing scenarios, instrument qualifications, failed/retest/seasonal cases and end-to-end application/rendered-report review; record unresolved contractual differences explicitly.

findings.title: Qualify immutable remedy and closure bytes rather than READY markers
findings.observed: R26 marks a defect RECTIFIED using an object with status READY but no provider version or observed-size receipt. Both remedy/close paths check object status and scope heuristics rather than the complete verified-byte predicates used by review/readiness.
findings.correction: Require verified immutable object identity, observed size/hash and applicable remedy metadata before accepting the evidence reference. At closure, verify the exact submitted remedy version and retain an independent verifier decision; do not require a fake engineering approval just to pass.
findings.acceptance: Test READY-only markers, wrong/missing version/hash/size, deleted/quarantined objects, changed evidence and same-size corruption. Keep current mandatory expected version and independent-verifier guards.

findings.title: Replace storage-key and first-asset heuristics with exact remedy scope
findings.observed: Remedy/close accept project/defect/asset identity inferred from object_key substrings or a LIMIT1 linked asset. Keys are routing metadata, not authoritative qualification, and a shared document can contain multiple asset links.
findings.correction: Persist explicit defect→remedy-version→project/asset bindings under composite constraints, with approved scope/reuse policy and full target-set validation. Preserve the exact remedy identity through independent closure.
findings.acceptance: Test misleading keys, shared multi-asset documents, wrong project/defect, missing positive binding and link changes after submission. Valid reused evidence works only with explicit applicable scope.

findings.title: Define post-handover defect policy without rewriting accepted closeout
findings.observed: R25 records a new defect in a CLOSED project. Warranty defects after handover can be legitimate, so this observation alone is not proof that recording must be forbidden. The service lacks an explicit policy distinguishing new warranty work from baseline-changing corrections and terminal-project states.
findings.correction: Define permitted post-handover defect creation/remedy/verification, shared locks and impact on current readiness/acceptance. Keep past accepted packages immutable; require formal reopening only where the approved policy changes the contractual baseline.
findings.acceptance: Test legitimate warranty defects, closed/archived/cancelled projects, concurrent final closure and new mandatory defects. Verify retained reads, customer notice and explicit reopening/acceptance impact.

findings.title: Enforce current assignee, party and resource authority for defect work
findings.observed: The service locks the defect but does not apply complete per-assignee/party/asset scope qualification. A project-level defect.manage capability alone is not evidence that a supplier contributor may remedy or verify every defect in that project.
findings.correction: Validate current task/party/resource eligibility and separation of duties at each create/assign/remedy/close transition. Keep the existing assignee/remedy-performer self-verification blocks and support explicit eligible delegation.
findings.acceptance: Use actual HTTP for narrowly assigned suppliers, wrong party/asset, unassigned members, revoked grants and independent qualified verifiers. All aliases, lists/counts and task links must follow the same scope.

findings.title: Persist assignment, remedy revisions and controlled reopen/waiver history
findings.observed: Current endpoints mainly create/remedy/close; a complete assignment/triage/reopen/authorized waiver and attachment revision workflow is absent. Repeated remedy submissions can replace the current evidence without a separate immutable remedy-attempt ledger.
findings.correction: Implement a reviewed defect state machine with responsible party/user, due/severity rules, versioned remedy attempts and independent decision history. Reopening/waiving needs explicit authority/reason and cannot erase prior closure evidence.
findings.acceptance: Test failed remedy, resubmission, independent rejection, reopen, concurrent assignment and overdue escalation. Work-item versions and history must identify the exact evidence/decision being acted on.

findings.title: Align defect severity, readiness and user-visible recovery
findings.observed: Creation maps MINOR/MAJOR to LOW/HIGH while consumers also reference legacy severities; unknown inputs silently default to MEDIUM. Operational and commercial readiness must use one approved mandatory-blocker policy, not incidental enum strings.
findings.correction: Validate and migrate a single severity/mandatory-blocker contract, expose typed actionable errors and synchronize responsible-user notices/tasks. Keep technical readiness and informational financial views distinct.
findings.acceptance: Test all supported/unknown severities, critical open/rectified/closed defects, legacy migration and package/close gates. Actual UI must submit required versions and preserve failed-state recovery.

findings.title: Accept genuine remedy and independent closure evidence
findings.observed: The audit fixtures establish a qualification defect and positive independence controls; they do not establish real repair, OEM workmanship or lawful customer closure.
findings.correction: Run representative real defect/remedy/rejection/closure journeys with independently reviewed evidence and qualified roles on the integrated candidate.
findings.acceptance: Include multi-asset evidence, repeat failure, customer warranty defect after handover and concurrency. Retain attributable remedy/verification history and acceptance impact.

findings.title: Remove active PDF actions in the actual dossier pipeline
findings.observed: R39 compiles a real three-page dossier from a harmless source with page-level AA/JavaScript; the final qpdf JSON still contains both dictionaries. No PDF viewer execution or exploit is claimed. The actual compiler does not invoke the separate sanitizer before copying pages.
findings.correction: Apply a canonical tested sanitization policy to verified source derivatives and the final artifact, including page/catalog/annotation/chained actions and attachments. Preserve originals and signed-byte provenance; never modify evidence silently or break genuine signatures without disclosure.
findings.acceptance: Test inert canaries for all action locations in compressed/uncompressed PDFs through actual worker compilation, then inspect final structure. Verify valid navigation/content remains and no active action survives under the approved policy.

findings.title: Unify sanitizer implementations and make evidence claims truthful
findings.observed: R40 calls sanitizeAndCheckPdfBomb, which returns safe=true and strippedScriptsCount=2 while the output retains page AA/JavaScript. The count is matched keys, not proven removals. This helper is not the live compiler sanitizer, so its success cannot certify generated dossiers.
findings.correction: Remove divergent safety paths or route them through one bounded implementation with explicit reject/remove outcomes. Derive removal diagnostics from verified before/after structure; test the actual selected runtime path and retain input/output digests.
findings.acceptance: For every supported PDF path, assert real output action absence, exact byte lineage, valid pages and truthful diagnostics. Do not label a scan/match count as sanitized content.

findings.title: Bound every PDF, image, Office and verifier resource path
findings.observed: Large dossier merging uses qpdf and source/output ceilings, which is positive. Some fallback/bookmark/image/Office paths load whole files or run parsers without OS isolation; bookmarks silently skip/fail for large or unsupported text. The browser verifier hashes each entire file in memory up to the archive size contract.
findings.correction: Define tested end-to-end page/object/byte/pixel/memory/time budgets for each supported path. Use constrained subprocesses/workers, robust font handling and an explicit capability policy for large outputs; do not silently omit required navigation.
findings.acceptance: Run large/compressed/scanned/mixed-format and non-Latin fixtures under measured memory/CPU limits and actual mobile verifier budgets. Fail clearly before publication when required output cannot be produced.

findings.title: Complete verified conversion and paired PDF/ZIP outputs
findings.observed: The actual package worker rejects non-PDF sources as PACKAGE_SOURCE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED. A standalone converter exists, but no complete safe source→derivative→reviewed package workflow connects it. Package generation publishes PDF; a project-wide portable archive is not the same frozen package ZIP/manifest contract.
findings.correction: Integrate supported format conversion with verified derivative lineage and explicit original attachments, then publish PDF plus paired ZIP/CSV/JSON manifest from the same frozen package selection. Keep unsupported formats honestly blocked until accepted.
findings.acceptance: Test approved photos/DOCX/XLSX/DWG policy, conversion failure, exact page ranges, original hashes, manifests and retry. PDF/ZIP must contain exactly the authorized frozen scope and retained originals.

findings.title: Preserve document and decision provenance in all generated content
findings.observed: Dossier input/output has useful version IDs and checksum/page-range controls, but cover/index schemas omit parts of the full required approval dates/history/asset register/waiver details and use current mutable project/contract names when the worker starts. Non-Latin text and blank signature boxes need honest semantics.
findings.correction: Freeze required names, assets/lineage, exact revision/decision/actor/time/method, waiver provenance and ordering in the package manifest. Render from that snapshot with reviewed fonts/layout; distinguish signature placeholders from verification.
findings.acceptance: Compare output extraction/visual review and manifest to real approved source records after project/name/contract changes. Verify all required index fields, dates, lineage, page ranges and warnings with no fabricated values.

findings.title: Pin archive consistency and independently retain authenticity evidence
findings.observed: Portable archives positively verify each source/version/hash and output readback and honestly disclaim signer authenticity. Export manifest tables are read across several statements; a consistent evidence/audit checkpoint and independently retained receipt are still needed for a reproducible legal archive.
findings.correction: Use a defined consistent snapshot/checkpoint for metadata and source selection, pin object versions, preserve approval/identity history and retain the canonical receipt outside the archive trust boundary. Do not claim whole-archive authenticity from a verifier shipped inside the same replaceable archive.
findings.acceptance: Race edits/reviews/export, replace the whole archive/verifier, alter one byte and omit/add files. Verify exact scope, external receipt/checkpoint consistency and truthful offline authenticity status.

findings.title: Make artifact retries, orphan cleanup and publication fail safely
findings.observed: Portable archive uses a session advisory lock and verifies completed replay. Package publication has a different job-ID ownership scheme; provider success before DB failure can orphan output versions. Download/retention validity depends on immutable non-null version receipts and reconciled storage facts.
findings.correction: Use per-attempt fenced ownership, durable output receipts and cleanup/reconciliation for failed publication. Validate provider capabilities and final artifact checks before READY; preserve retained completed versions and safe retry semantics.
findings.acceptance: Inject provider timeout/accepted upload, wrong/null version, corrupt body, lost DB commit and worker restart. No stale worker may publish success or delete another accepted artifact.

findings.title: Accept representative real dossiers and archives independently
findings.observed: Local PDF/archive fixtures prove mechanisms, not legal evidence acceptance, production S3 durability or large customer document compatibility.
findings.correction: Have domain/security reviewers inspect genuine representative generated PDFs/ZIPs, manifests, retained originals and independent receipts using the final worker/browser/storage setup.
findings.acceptance: Cover large mixed-source documents, genuine signed PDFs, malicious-action negatives, non-Latin text, wrong-scope/missing files, offline verification and retention/restore. Attach measured budgets and sanitized real provider receipts.

findings.title: Implement explicit package scope, preview and cancellation
findings.observed: The service input exposes excludedRequirementIds but does not apply it. There is no complete whole-project/category/assets/requirements scope, preflight page-count preview or cancellation API. Ignoring a supplied exclusion can export content the requester expected excluded.
findings.correction: Define and validate a typed scope contract, reject unsupported exclusions, and produce a frozen permission-filtered preview matching generation. Add explicit cancellable job states and clear policy for mandatory excluded work/partial packages.
findings.acceptance: Test each scope, unknown/hidden IDs, exclusions/reasons, preview→apply parity, stale preview and cancellation before/during/after provider publication. Partial output cannot satisfy full closure.

findings.title: Freeze one consistently qualified manifest under shared lifecycle locks
findings.observed: Readiness is checked before and again inside package creation using duplicated SQL; snapshot and requirement/evidence selection occur in additional statements without a shared project lock. These predicates can drift during concurrent baseline/review changes despite positive composite FKs and qualified-byte checks.
findings.correction: Use one canonical qualification/selection operation under the shared project/snapshot lock and appropriate snapshot isolation. Freeze exact requirement/evidence/decision/waiver facts and project metadata; make scope/expiry policy explicit at generation time.
findings.acceptance: Deterministically race snapshot import, waiver/review, document deletion, identity revalidation and closure against generation. Preview, frozen manifest and actual sources must be one coherent allowed version with no stale success.

findings.title: Use per-attempt worker ownership and recoverable generation state
findings.observed: The worker owner token is PACKAGE_JOB:<jobId>. A stalled BullMQ retry can reuse that job ID; a second process with the same owner is not excluded by the different-owner GENERATING check. Failure/retry behavior also needs a supported reset from FAILED, which is not a buildable state in the claim query.
findings.correction: Persist a unique per-attempt token/lease with heartbeat or bounded expiry and compare-and-set every side effect/publication. Implement authorized retry/cancel with durable output reconciliation, not status resetting without provenance.
findings.acceptance: Run two processes with the same logical job and different attempts, lease loss, stalled recovery, crash after upload and failure redrive. Only the current attempt publishes READY and counters/events settle once.

findings.title: Reject non-immutable and unqualified artifact receipts
findings.observed: Package publication/download require nonempty version/hash/size facts, which is positive, but truthy VersionId="null" is not rejected as an immutable identity. R44 demonstrates the same receipt defect in the upload storage adapter. Provider checksum/HEAD guarantees require real capability acceptance.
findings.correction: Use shared immutable-receipt validation and provider checksum/version verification for source/output and download. Preserve source digests and retain complete output lineage; never infer versioning from a truthy sentinel.
findings.acceptance: Test missing/null sentinel version, absent observed size, hash/HEAD mismatch, corrupt readback and accepted-package download. Valid immutable output remains downloadable after submission/acceptance.

findings.title: Connect approved source formats and complete package contents
findings.observed: The worker rejects every non-PDF source, while required output includes assets/lineage, full approval dates/history and paired originals/manifest. A successful PDF build alone is not the full FR-HND-002/004 contract.
findings.correction: Implement the G25 conversion/content fixes once and make package readiness include all required artifacts/sections. Keep explicit purpose FULL_HANDOVER versus RA_BILL and preserve the existing ban on RA acceptance as final handover.
findings.acceptance: Use real reviewed mixed-format scope and inspect PDF, ZIP, manifest and index against frozen records. Missing required content or conversion failure must produce a clear non-READY state.

findings.title: Apply one generation capacity, purpose and lifecycle contract
findings.observed: Full generation uses a hardcoded monthly quota and accepts only a limited input contract; RA generation is a separate writer. Full requests are serialized by the quota row today, so this audit does not claim two full requests necessarily race MAX(version_no). Other writers and post-close generation still need shared policy.
findings.correction: Use G18 authoritative entitlements and shared project/purpose/version allocation for every generator. Define retained historical regeneration versus new contractual revisions and permitted lifecycle states; bind retries to durable commands.
findings.acceptance: Race full/RA/retry requests, final capacity, archive/closure and downgrade. Verify unique purpose/version, no double charge and no RA/partial package used for full acceptance.

findings.title: Expose truthful progress, failure and retained artifact recovery
findings.observed: QUEUED/GENERATING/FAILED fields exist, but a complete progress/cancel/retry and failed-artifact recovery journey is missing. An optional bookmark failure or unsupported source must not be presented as complete contractual output.
findings.correction: Expose typed progress and safe failure/retry actions from durable job state, including requested scope/artifacts and cancellation outcome. Keep prior accepted versions available under explicit policy without silently substituting stale output for a new failed request.
findings.acceptance: Run actual UI for slow build, unsupported file, provider failure, reload, stale worker, cancel and retry. Show committed status and correct current versus historical download links.

findings.title: Accept full generation-to-closure integrity on one candidate
findings.observed: R33 positively rejects generation with an unconfigured baseline. Fixtures do not establish a real complete contractual package; current closure safeguards must remain intact.
findings.correction: After repairs, run reviewed baseline→verified evidence→package→required recipients→full acceptance→closure on one integrated head with actual approved artifacts.
findings.acceptance: Include changed baseline/expiry/revalidation after generation, partial and RA packages, failed new revision, required-recipient negatives and retained downloads. No status-only or synthetic baseline shortcut is allowed.

findings.title: Separate prepared submission, verified dispatch and recipient decision
findings.observed: createSubmission records status SUBMITTED and returns that while recipients are PENDING_DELIVERY and only SUBMISSION_PREPARED is emitted. The pending-recipient state is honest, but no complete dispatch/receipt/reconciliation workflow makes the submission actually delivered.
findings.correction: Define prepared/queued/accepted-by-provider/delivered/failed/decided states and implement recipient-specific durable delivery with G20 safe templates and receipts. Preserve nonblocking business intent while presenting truthful external delivery status.
findings.acceptance: Test absent provider, accepted-timeout, bounce, resend, crash and receipt replay. UI, audit and recipient links must distinguish prepared intent from delivered or legally accepted handover.

findings.title: Validate actual required recipients and submission identity
findings.observed: R31 repeats preparation and produces two submissions while the package remains READY. This is a service/state observation, not proof of two commits for a reused HTTP idempotency key. Recipient flags/party IDs are weakly typed and duplicate or ineligible required parties can create unusable acceptance flows.
findings.correction: Validate canonical current counterparties/destinations/boolean flags and a reviewed required-approver set, with stable submission command identity and an explicit resend/new-submission policy. Prevent ambiguous duplicates and transition package/submission state coherently.
findings.acceptance: Test string false versus false, duplicate party/email, no required approvers, wrong/inactive party, retry with same/different command and explicit resend. No accidental duplicate or zero-approver dead end should be reported as completed.

findings.title: Bind recipient consent to the exact reviewed package and evidence
findings.observed: The acceptance command correctly rejects internal-member impersonation (R32), checks current independent party authority and prevents repeat terminal decisions. It does not provide a complete immutable receipt/declaration/version-precondition contract for exactly what the recipient reviewed.
findings.correction: Persist exact package/version/checksum/scope, recipient principal/delegation/proof time and informed decision declaration. Make stale or historical decisions explicit and ensure acceptance of an older package never certifies the current corrected package.
findings.acceptance: Test wrong party/hash/revision, new package after link issue, revoked proof, replay, historical physical evidence and concurrent decisions. Preserve required-recipient and full-purpose checks.

findings.title: Make exception/rejection outcomes and follow-up work complete
findings.observed: Acceptance-with-exceptions creates a pending change request, but the complete affected-item mapping, responsible successor, evidence and approval/application journey is not implemented. A generic title/doc-type list is not a controlled change to the current baseline.
findings.correction: Bind exception items to frozen package requirements, validate deltas and responsible parties, and route follow-up through G06/G07 approved impact control. Preserve partial acceptance distinctly; never infer full closure or warranty trigger from it.
findings.acceptance: Test unknown/stale/duplicate items, rejected follow-up, multiple required/optional recipients and later corrected submissions. Verify visible actionable work and immutable original customer response.

findings.title: Enforce lifecycle and concurrency across preparation and response
findings.observed: Submission methods lock package/submission/recipient rows but do not share one project/baseline lifecycle boundary with generation/closure. Receipt of a legitimate post-close historical response needs a different policy from changing current contractual acceptance.
findings.correction: Define allowed prepare/resend/respond/withdraw/correct transitions, current version preconditions and deterministic lock order with closure. Preserve history and invalidate current acceptance only through an explicit reviewed transition.
findings.acceptance: Race generation, new snapshot, closure, withdrawal and recipient response. Verify no stale current acceptance, deadlock, partial recipient update or hidden reopening of an accepted package.

findings.title: Complete recipient-side viewing and response UX
