findings.observed: The guest application lacks a complete recipient-specific preview/download/declaration/accept/reject/exception journey with real delivery recovery. Backend acceptance guards alone do not deliver the customer workflow.
findings.correction: Provide current verified-party access to the exact submitted package, safe review context, required reason/evidence fields, explicit decision confirmation and a durable receipt. Keep customer identity, tenant and revision visible without leaking internal notes.
findings.acceptance: Use actual customer/consultant browsers for expired/forwarded links, wrong recipient, scope changes, failed download/submit, mobile accessibility and reload after committed response.

findings.title: Preserve immutable decision/export records and safe corrections
findings.observed: Current decision rows update status/remarks with a one-time guard, but there is no complete separately authorized correction/withdrawal and export receipt workflow for disputed or historical customer outcomes. Delivery, acceptance and cryptographic signing are distinct facts.
findings.correction: Use append-only decision/correction records with reasons, exact subject and independent authority. Define retention and safe party-visible receipt/export projection; do not overwrite prior factual customer responses.
findings.acceptance: Test disputed/withdrawn/corrected decisions, audit export, retained downloads and cross-party privacy. Verify older facts remain attributable while current aggregate state follows approved policy.

findings.title: Accept genuine customer handover and recovery operationally
findings.observed: Synthetic guest principals and fixture decisions do not establish lawful recipient authority, real delivery or customer acceptance. Current project closure correctly requires matching latest full package and required recipients; retain that boundary.
findings.correction: Obtain accountable customer/legal/domain approval and real end-to-end recipient evidence on the integrated head before relying on acceptance for production closeout.
findings.acceptance: Attach verified party/delegation, exact reviewed package, actual delivery, required/optional recipient outcomes, partial/rejected/resubmitted cases and recovery/retention evidence.

findings.title: Distinguish recorded OEM claims from verified warranty confirmation
findings.observed: R27 records CONFIRMED coverage through a contractor service call with no OEM evidence object, even on a CLOSED project. Matching the stored basis is enough to set dates; a caller-entered OEM reference is not independent coverage evidence.
findings.correction: Use explicit reported/pending/verified/disputed warranty states and require qualified OEM/contract evidence and reviewer provenance before authoritative confirmation/extension. Support legitimate post-handover warranty records without rewriting accepted closeout.
findings.acceptance: Test no/unverified/wrong-asset evidence, real confirmed evidence, unauthorized extension and historical post-handover updates. Display recorded assertions separately from accepted coverage.

findings.title: Detect same-basis date conflicts and version extensions
findings.observed: R28 stores two CONFIRMED events with different start dates but the same basis; COALESCE keeps the older asset date. Only basis mismatch creates DISPUTED, so the event ledger and asset coverage can disagree without a surfaced conflict.
findings.correction: Validate date order/precision and compare both basis and dates against the authoritative accepted coverage. Version extensions/corrections with qualified evidence and reason; never silently overwrite or simultaneously certify incompatible periods.
findings.acceptance: Test conflicting starts/ends, backdated and future records, extension before coverage, claim events and concurrent confirmation. Asset dates, events, alerts and exports must show one explained current coverage state.

findings.title: Bind warranty events to actual asset and contractual triggers
findings.observed: Asset creation accepts warranty dates and a default HANDOVER basis; registration/confirmation can populate them independently. Real commissioning, acceptance, supply and replacement events need explicit trigger/evidence linkage, not inference from administrative project closure.
findings.correction: Define reviewed trigger authority and exact source event/version per asset, preserving existing accepted dates and OEM terms. Carry coverage/claim responsibility through replacement lineage with a controlled policy for new equipment.
findings.acceptance: Test each basis, missing/disputed trigger, existing-date precedence, partial acceptance, replacement and administrative closure. No status string or project close timestamp may manufacture OEM coverage.

findings.title: Complete warranty/claim management and scoped UI
findings.observed: The API records events and lists them, but does not deliver the full claim/responsible-party/evidence/decision/extension workflow or equipment-wise user recovery and reporting. Generic eventType values do not implement a managed OEM claim.
findings.correction: Implement versioned claim lifecycle, deadlines, contacts, attachments, responsible party, qualified decisions and safe warranty register/asset views. Apply current project/asset scope and preserve immutable history.
findings.acceptance: Run actual UI/API claim→OEM response→resolution, wrong party/scope, rejected claim, changed equipment and reload/error cases; verify original evidence and decision provenance.

findings.title: Schedule warranty/DLP obligations from qualified dates
findings.observed: Required 30/14/7/1 expiry reminders are not a complete implemented producer. An unresolved or disputed warranty date cannot safely drive expiry/retention tasks or imply claim eligibility.
findings.correction: Integrate the G20 reminder fix with qualified asset/OEM/DLP dates, current PM/asset owner and durable dedup/cancellation. Separate OEM warranty, defect liability and evidence retention clocks.
findings.acceptance: Use controllable clocks for all offsets, leap/month boundaries, revised/disputed dates, replacement, completed claims and missed worker runs. No duplicate or inaccurate expiry notice may be sent.

findings.title: Obtain real OEM/contract warranty acceptance
findings.observed: Local date/event fixtures are not real OEM registration, contractual trigger verification or a warranted repair. Legal coverage and customer/OEM operational policy need accountable acceptance.
findings.correction: Validate representative OEM/contract coverage, replacement and DLP cases with domain/legal reviewers and real application evidence on the final head.
findings.acceptance: Attach sanitized genuine supporting records, date/basis conflict resolution, claim outcomes and reminder/recovery results. Keep unverified assertions visibly pending/disputed.

findings.title: Verify Form16A bytes and authority before marking TDS reconciled
findings.observed: R29 marks a TDS item RECONCILED using a PENDING storage object with no verified bytes. reconcileForm16aTdsCertificate updates the reference/object/status without the complete certificate qualification or current invoice/customer/tax-period review.
findings.correction: Validate same-tenant immutable scanned certificate/version, invoice/customer/FY/period scope and authorized finance review. Record a versioned reconciliation decision; a supplied object ID/reference alone must not certify a tax deduction.
findings.acceptance: Test pending/quarantined/wrong-tenant/wrong-period certificates, duplicate/replaced certificates, invalid references and independent positive evidence. Status and annual summary must reflect actual approved reconciliation.

findings.title: Constrain deductions to approved invoice/tax facts and cumulative balances
findings.observed: R30 records 999999 paise of TDS against an invoice total of 118 paise. Per-row DB positivity/rate checks do not validate section/rate applicability, cumulative deductions, duplicates, invoice state or recoverable reconciliation.
findings.correction: Use reviewed tax configuration and locked invoice/deduction ledgers with exact integer paise, idempotent external references and approved correction/credit workflows. Validate cumulative amounts and jurisdiction/section facts rather than accepting arbitrary rate/amount input.
findings.acceptance: Test multiple concurrent deductions, over-deduction, wrong rate/section, void/refunded invoices, duplicate receipts and corrections. Preserve legitimate partial deductions without double-counting.

findings.title: Consolidate invoice issuance under reviewed configuration
findings.observed: The routed BillingService path hardcodes GST/SAC and an exemption declaration; a separate configurable Rule46 method is not the routed canonical path. Invoice issuance is default-OFF, a positive safety gate, and must remain disabled until corrected/accepted.
findings.correction: Use one typed invoice service driven by approved effective-dated supplier/buyer/place-of-supply/tax/rounding configuration, immutable numbering and legal disclosures. Validate all monetary/date/identity fields and issue corrections through credit/debit records.
findings.acceptance: Test real routed disabled behavior first, then approved intra/inter-state, exemption/applicability, concurrent numbering, large integers and finalized invoice immutability. Never turn the flag on to make tests pass.

findings.title: Make IRP/provider side effects durable and mandatory applicability fail closed
findings.observed: The configurable invoice helper calls GSP while holding the DB transaction/sequence and only generates IRN when a client object is present. An enabled mandatory IRP policy without a client can fall through as NOT_APPLICABLE. This helper is not a completed live routed integration.
findings.correction: Define authoritative applicability and fail honestly when mandatory provider capability is missing. Persist issue intent/provider attempt/outcome and reconcile timeout/rollback with provider idempotency rather than retaining a global sequence lock across network I/O.
findings.acceptance: Use provider sandbox for accepted-timeout, duplicate invoice, missing client, rejection/cancellation and DB failure after acknowledgement. No ISSUED/NOT_APPLICABLE state may conceal an unresolved mandatory IRN.

findings.title: Do not label informational retention as authoritative payment eligibility
findings.observed: getCommercialReadiness accepts any historical ACCEPTED submission, lacks the current full-package/recipient/checksum closure contract, and gives 100% satisfaction when no mandatory requirements exist. It uses project money/default retention while other views aggregate contracts. FR-CNT-003 says these values are informational.
findings.correction: Reuse canonical current readiness and matching latest full-handover acceptance for technical indicators, while separately exposing reviewed contractual financial facts and unknowns. Remove unsupported ELIGIBLE/payment-release claims or qualify them through an accepted finance workflow.
findings.acceptance: Test no baseline/unknown value, old/RA/partial acceptance, new obligations, multiple contracts and warranty defects. Dashboards/exports must not imply earned money or an automatic legal release from status strings.

findings.title: Complete finance history, documents and annual exports
findings.observed: Current billing lists/invoice/TDS endpoints do not deliver the complete approved downloadable invoice, annual TDS summary, payment/refund/credit-note reconciliation and actor/reason history. Readable rows are not a complete auditable financial product.
findings.correction: Implement the approved MVP invoice/TDS outputs and immutable finance ledger/receipt exports. Scope V1 refunds/proration and V2 accounting export explicitly, keeping incomplete actions disabled and visible as unavailable.
findings.acceptance: Run actual finance UI/API issuance/view/download/TDS/correction/export with role/tenant negatives, retries and unknown provider state. Compare every paise and tax disclosure to reviewed expected records.

findings.title: Integrate payment settlement with entitlement and notification ledgers
findings.observed: Raw webhook HMAC/inbox and processed=false are truthful controls; automatic settlement/fulfilment remains disabled. G18 already records the missing subscription state machine. Finance must not interpret received provider JSON or caller notes as settled money/tenant authority.
findings.correction: Implement one provider-reference reconciliation contract with server-owned tenant/invoice/subscription mapping, duplicate/order handling, pending/failed/refunded states and durable safe dunning notifications. Preserve signature verification and restricted inbox privileges.
findings.acceptance: Run real sandbox replay/out-of-order/timeout/refund and provider outage tests through finance and entitlement ledgers. Statements, quota and customer notices must agree without fake paid states.

findings.title: Obtain accountable finance, tax and provider release acceptance
findings.observed: Neither code labels nor fixtures certify current GST/TDS/e-invoicing treatment, lawful invoice disclosure, genuine settlement or contractual retention release. No live financial issuance/charging is authorized by this audit.
findings.correction: Have accountable finance/legal/provider reviewers accept current configuration and operational reconciliation on the integrated candidate before enabling gated capabilities.
findings.acceptance: Attach approved scenarios, real sandbox receipts, integer-ledger reconciliation, invoice/certificate outputs, failure/rollback recovery and named review evidence. Keep production flags off until owner-authorized release.

findings.title: Complete supported product journeys against the real application
findings.observed: The frontend exposes selected project/evidence actions but lacks complete, recoverable setup, assignment, guest, commissioning, handover and finance journeys. The six passing existing application browser contracts comprise two live authentication flows, two function contracts and two mocked-response browser flows; none certifies full Phase3/4 business completion.
findings.correction: Define the supported MVP journey/role matrix and implement each promised step with real API contracts, current context, validation, authorization-aware actions and observable completion. Explicitly exclude approved future features instead of exposing inert or misleading controls.
findings.acceptance: Run organisation→project→approved baseline→asset→upload/scan→review→handover→external acceptance→warranty/finance journeys through browser/API/worker on one integrated SHA, including denial, stale version and interrupted-operation branches.

findings.title: Share response schemas and handle narrowed authority DTOs
findings.observed: The audit page calls e.hash.slice and e.prev_hash.slice on assumed fields. The separately proposed G03 metadata-only audit DTO omits those hashes, so integration needs an explicit versioned contract rather than restoring excessive audit data. Project-directory/summary contract defects are already recorded in Phase2.
findings.correction: Generate or share current typed response schemas, parse boundary responses and render missing/denied fields safely. Resolve Phase2 frontend DTO items once and add compatibility checks for the integrated G03 proposal; keep full audit integrity material behind the correct authority.
findings.acceptance: Test every route with actual current and proposed API DTOs, empty/null/denied fields, malformed responses, context switches and network failures. No render crash, invented field, unauthorized hash disclosure or stale tenant content.

findings.title: Make action visibility and server decisions coherent
findings.observed: The project screen renders many mutation controls from generic local state and relies on server errors/alerts. A complete per-action current membership, resource-scope, lifecycle and external-party capability contract is not represented consistently in the client.
findings.correction: Expose bounded server-derived action capabilities and reasons, invalidate them after context/authority changes, and use consistent pending/disabled/error states. Keep server authorization authoritative and avoid discovering permitted targets by mutation attempts.
findings.acceptance: Exercise Owner/PM/Site/reviewer/customer/supplier and narrow/read-only scopes across all visible actions. Revocation, another-tab context switch and lifecycle change must promptly remove stale actions and handle final server denial safely.

findings.title: Deliver honest scoped search, reporting and completion views
findings.observed: There is no dedicated complete metadata-search/reporting API module in the application module graph. Local page filters, equipment-matrix rows and status-derived dashboard values do not fulfill global scoped metadata search, authoritative reports or all promised exports.
findings.correction: Implement the approved MVP search/report endpoints with tenant/resource filtering before pagination/counts, stable queries and actual evidence qualification. Clearly label partial/local views and unavailable metrics; remove fabricated or inferred business completion.
findings.acceptance: Test multi-project and narrow-scope searches, hidden-target counts, large pagination, stale evidence and exports. Compare report totals and selected versions to the canonical G07/G09/G11/G14 readiness contract.

findings.title: Generate robust spreadsheet downloads with safe cells
findings.observed: The project CSV helper quotes cells but does not neutralize formula-leading user text, and builds a data URI using encodeURI. Reserved characters such as # can change URI interpretation. This is source-confirmed; no spreadsheet exploit was executed.
findings.correction: Use a tested UTF-8 CSV/Excel serializer with a deliberate formula-cell policy, correct quoting/newlines and Blob object URLs revoked after download. Preserve exact money/unit data and current authorized export scope.
findings.acceptance: Round-trip apostrophes, commas, quotes, CR/LF, Unicode, #, percent signs and formula-leading cells through supported spreadsheet consumers. Check filenames, large-file limits, scoped rows and integer totals.

findings.title: Verify accessibility and mobile usability on actual workflows
findings.observed: Build and authentication browser checks provide no complete keyboard, screen-reader, focus-management, contrast, validation-announcement or field-device usability acceptance for the product. Custom dialogs, dense tables and alert-based errors need end-to-end verification.
findings.correction: Implement accessible names, keyboard/focus/escape behavior, live errors, field associations, semantic status, responsive tables and reachable touch targets in each supported journey. Use automated checks plus accountable manual assistive-technology testing.
findings.acceptance: Attach keyboard-only and screen-reader results for login/MFA, upload, review, guest response, waiver, package and offline recovery; test small screens/zoom and failure states. Do not claim accessibility certification from automated scans alone.

findings.title: Make asynchronous failures and retries visible and recoverable
findings.observed: The project screen silently ignores some fetch failures and converts warranty/defect request failures to empty arrays, while many mutations use blocking alerts. Empty data can therefore mean failed loading rather than an actual absence of work.
findings.correction: Model loading/empty/denied/failed/stale states distinctly, preserve user input, show actionable errors and retries, and bind mutation retries to correct idempotency/version contracts. Poll or subscribe to long-running job outcomes and invalidate caches after authoritative transitions.
findings.acceptance: Inject API timeouts, 401/403/409/429/5xx, lost responses and slow scan/package jobs. The UI must retain input, avoid duplicate commands and never present failed loading as zero defects or successful completion.

findings.title: Obtain integrated user-journey and accessibility release acceptance
findings.observed: No complete customer/contractor/field acceptance or full Phase3/4 browser journey was demonstrated here. Passing a frontend build and the six existing contracts cannot supply that evidence.
findings.correction: Have product, accessibility and representative users accept the implemented MVP scope on the deployable integrated SHA. Record explicit exclusions, genuine outcomes, error recovery and support guidance.
findings.acceptance: Attach traceable browser results, human usability/accessibility review, supported device matrix and issue dispositions. All user-visible critical paths and authorization negatives must pass before release.

findings.title: Refresh expired multipart upload URLs during offline replay
findings.observed: B01 executes the actual queue module in Chromium/IndexedDB against a loopback provider fixture: after an expired URL, two drains repeat two PUT 403 failures with one intent, zero refresh calls and no completion. The foreground upload component has refresh logic; the offline queue does not.
findings.correction: Use a shared bounded multipart replay client that refreshes authoritative outstanding-part URLs when eligible, preserves part receipts and handles expired/aborted intents with explicit safe restart. Never reuse stale URLs indefinitely or move a draft to another actor.
findings.acceptance: Expire URLs between parts and across reload/offline intervals; cover signing/provider 403 distinctions, revoked intent, changed tenant and already-completed parts. Resume to verified READY once without losing the original.

findings.title: Serialize queue drains across triggers and tabs
findings.observed: B02 runs two concurrent drains of the actual queue module: both issue PUT and completion requests for one queued file. Stable backend idempotency keys are a positive control; this fixture proves duplicate network commands, not duplicate committed document versions.
findings.correction: Use an atomic durable per-item lease/generation and a cross-tab drain coordinator, with expiry and fenced checkpoint updates. Recheck the current actor and intent before every external write; retain backend deduplication as an independent fence.
findings.acceptance: Race online/visibility/service-worker/manual triggers, two tabs, tab crashes and actor rotation. One active sender owns a part/complete transition and recovery cannot overwrite newer receipts or remove another actor’s draft.

findings.title: Reconcile processing and classify replay failures durably
findings.observed: After bounded status polling the queue retains the original Blob and marks PROCESSING, correctly avoiding a false success. There is no complete ongoing reconciliation scheduler/backoff/error taxonomy; another foreground trigger may be required to learn a later scan result.
findings.correction: Persist explicit upload/verify/retry/blocked/quarantined terminal states, resume authoritative status checks independently of new uploads, and distinguish recoverable transport/provider failures from authorization or malware rejection. Bound retry attempts and support safe user cancellation.
findings.acceptance: Exercise scans longer than the poll window, browser reload, delayed clean/quarantine, provider timeout and completed intent replay. UI state must converge to the server result with durable receipts and no blind re-upload of rejected evidence.

findings.title: Provide explicit recovery for blocked drafts after authentication changes
findings.observed: Existing actor-partition/session-generation fences correctly stop stale drafts after context rotation. The product lacks a complete inspect/recover/discard workflow for a legitimate same-person draft that remains BLOCKED_SCOPE after reauthentication; automatic actor rebinding would weaken the existing isolation.
findings.correction: Provide an authenticated recovery UI that shows the original tenant/project/requirement, rechecks live authority and obtains explicit confirmation before any supported same-identity rebind. Never transfer drafts to another identity or silently revive revoked grants.
findings.acceptance: Cover logout/login same actor, different actor, tenant switch, revoked membership, changed requirement and expired guest grant. Authorized recovery retains bytes/receipts; unauthorized drafts remain inaccessible and safely removable according to retention policy.

findings.title: Bound local evidence retention, storage failures and draft visibility
findings.observed: Queued original Blobs and receipts have no complete user-visible inventory, quota/TTL and secure discard policy. IndexedDB quota/eviction/private-mode failures can defeat capture. The separate generic draft-storage helper is currently unused; this audit does not claim an active cross-user leak from that helper.
findings.correction: Implement bounded per-actor storage accounting, explicit persistence/error indications, original-file retention/discard policy and clean cancellation. Partition or retire generic draft helpers before use; avoid storing provider secrets or sensitive API responses in service-worker caches.
findings.acceptance: Test low quota, denied persistence, eviction, failed transactions, logout and crash. Show whether bytes are actually durable, preserve unsynced work when possible and never claim zero loss without demonstrated device support.

findings.title: Respect mobile memory budgets while preserving original evidence
findings.observed: computeBrowserFileSha256 materializes a whole Blob in memory. Large queued files, PDF hashing and concurrent drains lack demonstrated low-memory device budgets. The optional image-compression helper is not invoked by enqueue; silently invoking it would alter original evidence.
findings.correction: Use bounded streaming/chunk hashing and worker execution where supported, explicit per-device limits and controlled concurrency. Preserve originals; expose any compression as an optional clearly identified derivative with provenance and original hash.
findings.acceptance: Measure peak memory and responsiveness on supported low-memory devices at declared limits, including cancellation and multiple files. Original SHA-256 and stored bytes must match exactly across interrupted retries.

findings.title: Keep the shipped queue and offline claims within the approved scope

source.symbol: MVP does not support offline work

findings.observed: 11-UI-UX-SPECIFICATION.md explicitly excludes offline work from MVP while requiring transient-loss tolerance. The service worker safely avoids API/presigned-URL caching; sync merely notifies existing windows and cannot itself drain a closed app. These are limits to communicate, not grounds to mandate a full offline field-work product in MVP.
findings.correction: Document and test the actual supported transient-loss/queued-upload contract, including the need to reopen the app. Remove unconditional background/offline promises and preserve the current cache isolation. Full offline notes/assets/defects and conflict resolution require an approved later scope decision.
findings.acceptance: On supported browsers, test transient loss, airplane mode, no open windows, unsupported Background Sync and stale context. Distinguish saved locally, uploaded and verified; show connectivity requirements. Full offline capture is optional unless explicitly included in the release scope.

findings.title: Accept real-device interruption and provider recovery evidence
findings.observed: The two new browser observations use actual queue/IndexedDB code with loopback network fixtures. They are reproducible mechanics, not real S3 acceptance, mobile operating-system survival or complete API/worker synchronization tests.
findings.correction: Run the corrected queue against the integrated actual API/scanner/versioned storage on supported field devices and browsers with deliberate network/process interruptions.
findings.acceptance: Attach real provider part/checksum/version receipts, server deduplication, low-storage results, device/browser versions, cross-actor negatives and recovery after process termination. Independently verify original bytes and final qualified state.

findings.title: Make incident containment effective without weakening evidence constraints
findings.observed: R45 executes the actual RB-09 CLI against an APPROVED document version in a disposable database. Its file_status update fails SQLSTATE 23514 and rolls back, leaving READY. The script updates only document_versions despite its storage-object comment, accepts weak arguments/default reasons, uses migrator authority and may print success without checking a matching target.
findings.correction: Implement constrained break-glass identity and validated org/target/reason inputs, explicit dry run and target counts. Reconcile review/evidence state legally within invariants, quarantine backing objects, revoke future downloads and invalidate affected packages/acceptances as policy requires, preserving history and an attributable incident event.
findings.acceptance: Execute runbooks in isolated approved/rejected/missing-target and multi-tenant scenarios, with injected failure and replay. Verify actual object/version/package containment and truthful committed outcomes; retain the independent approval constraints.

findings.title: Complete and validate deployable infrastructure and runtime isolation
findings.observed: Terraform supplies partial database/bucket/host resources but not a complete deployable VPC/subnet/security-group/TLS/application-service/secrets/observability/remote-state contract. Local compose starts supporting infrastructure, not the full production app. No terraform executable was available for a validated plan in this audit.
findings.correction: Provide reviewed environment-specific infrastructure, least-privilege app/migrator/worker/ops roles, encrypted versioned storage and secrets rotation, private data-plane networking, HTTPS ingress and reproducible application/worker startup. Pin provider/image dependencies and protect state.
findings.acceptance: Run formatter/validator/security review and a reviewed plan in a disposable staging account, then demonstrate network/IAM negatives, TLS, scanner fail-closed behavior and worker boot. Do not apply to production as part of this documentation audit.

findings.title: Implement deployment, migration and rollback as a real release pipeline
findings.observed: The workflow named deploy.yml builds and tests but does not deploy the application. It does not establish immutable promoted artifacts, environment approval, safe schema sequencing, staged smoke verification or rehearsed application rollback.
findings.correction: Create a gated pipeline that promotes the same pinned images/artifacts, runs migrator identity once with immutable applied migrations, validates compatibility, deploys workers/API/web, performs independent health/business smoke checks and records rollout/rollback evidence.
findings.acceptance: Rehearse failed migration, partial rollout, worker backlog, unhealthy release and rollback on staging. Verify old/new app compatibility, no duplicated jobs and an auditable SHA/image/config manifest; production execution requires the normal release authorization.

findings.title: Prove complete backup and restore with consistent checkpoints
findings.observed: The restore drill compares restored counts to a live source after dump, which can change concurrently. It lacks complete cleanup on failure and verifies database/object metadata rather than actual S3-version recovery. A database count/hash check does not demonstrate physical evidence restore, PITR, KMS recovery or externally anchored audit continuity.
findings.correction: Use a consistent source snapshot/checkpoint, safe failure cleanup, access-controlled encrypted artifacts, verified physical versioned-object restoration and audit-chain continuity including genesis/anchor checks. Define retention, deletion/legal-hold compatibility, RPO/RTO and tested recovery credentials.
findings.acceptance: In an isolated recovery environment restore from an actual backup/PITR plus object versions, compare bytes/digests and qualified manifests, recover keys and verify download/worker/browser flows. Record measured RPO/RTO and outage response; never run this drill against production without its own operational authorization.

findings.title: Demonstrate operational capacity, alerts and dependency failure recovery
findings.observed: Green unit tests and /health are not measured production capacity or operational acceptance. There is no attached integrated load/soak evidence for scan/PDF/archive concurrency, database pools, local disks, provider outages, queue recovery or alert delivery to an accountable operator.
findings.correction: Define supported workload/SLO/resource budgets, bound job concurrency and temporary storage, add actionable secret-free metrics/alerts and rehearse provider/Redis/Postgres/scanner failure. Retain fail-closed evidence qualification and map each alarm to a tested runbook.
findings.acceptance: Attach load/soak and recovery results on production-like limits, alert receipts, queue lag/dead-letter recovery, timeout/cancellation cleanup and owner escalation. Readiness should distinguish service availability from accepted business evidence.

findings.title: Make CI and end-to-end verification cover real production claims
findings.observed: The clean candidate suite, typecheck/build, security and RBAC checks pass. New targeted probes still reproduce critical defects. Some browser checks are mocked/function contracts and configuration checks do not validate actual provider behavior; passing totals must not be described as a full product E2E release.
findings.correction: Add meaningful regression tests for the reproduced invariants and full real-service role/journey tests. Keep fixture/mechanics tests labeled; verify migration/RLS privileges, worker restarts, provider contracts, accessibility and actual release artifacts without weakening assertions or injecting fake domain evidence.
findings.acceptance: On the integrated SHA, publish test inventory and exact commands/results with real versus fixture boundaries, plus negative/concurrency cases for R37/R38/R39/R42/R43/R45 and B01/B02. Verify CI checks the application tree it will promote.

findings.title: Deliver the scoped platform administration contract
findings.observed: The main application module graph has no complete dedicated platform-admin workflow fulfilling the administrative requirements. Migrator-powered incident scripts and a read-only audit page do not supply controlled tenant/account support, break-glass access and independently reviewable administration.
findings.correction: Implement the approved MVP administration surface with separate limited privileges, reason/target validation, short-lived authorized elevation, tenant isolation, immutable operator events and independent review. Explicitly disable any unsupported administrative feature. Customer-content break-glass FR-ADM-002 is V1: keep it disabled in an MVP release unless separately approved and implemented; this audit does not mandate V1 scope.
findings.acceptance: Test cross-tenant lookup/mutation negatives, support read scopes, approval/elevation expiry, replay and audit integrity using an operator identity separate from app and migrator. Demonstrate safe account/tenant recovery without ordinary users gaining platform powers.

findings.title: Reconcile retention, legal hold and operational deletion across artifacts
findings.observed: Archive retention, soft deletion, physical object lifecycle, temporary compiler files, incident quarantine and backups need one accepted retention/legal-hold contract. An API soft-delete outcome or bucket lifecycle setting alone does not establish lawful complete deletion or preserved evidentiary history.
findings.correction: Complete the Phase1/2 retention and deletion items once, enumerate all replicas/artifacts/receipts, enforce legal hold before purge and implement observable resumable authorized purge with least privilege. Preserve immutable audit tombstones and avoid unsigned repair of historical evidence.
findings.acceptance: Test hold acquisition during scheduled deletion, partial provider failure, restore-after-delete policy, object versions, derived packages, local queue retention and backup expiry. Obtain accountable privacy/legal acceptance before enabling irreversible purge.

findings.title: Require one integrated, independently accepted production release
findings.observed: The app proposal, separate G03 proposal, Phase1/2 audit branches and this documentation branch are divergent heads. This audit intentionally does not integrate or certify them. No finite code audit can guarantee absence of every defect or replace real engineering, tax, provider, security and operational acceptance.
findings.correction: Fix and reconcile all applicable Phase1–5 items, formally approve documented MVP exclusions, integrate on one immutable candidate and obtain named independent product/security/HVAC/finance/operations review. Freeze exact sources, migrations, artifacts, configurations and evidence for a go/no-go decision.
findings.acceptance: All applicable P0/P1 work and material regressions must be closed by evidence on that candidate; external gates need genuine receipts and accountable signatures. Re-run integrated security/functional/E2E/restore/load acceptance and monitor a controlled rollout before calling the product production ready.
